This petition is filed by the Petitioner against Respondent for the relief of compensation under Sec.166 of the M.V.Act 1989.
2.

The brief facts of case of the Petitioner is that:
That on 12.03.2022 at about 5.30 p.m. petitioner was slowly and cautiously riding the cycle on the 11 th Cross, 1st Main, Muneshweara Block, Laggere, Bengaluru, at that time, driver of Xent bearing Reg.No.KA-546359 came on wrong direction in rash and negligent manner and dashed against his bicycle, as a result of which, petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, he was SCCH-5 shifted to Sanjeevini Hospital, wherein he took treatment as inpatient, for which,
spent an amount of Rs.8,00,000/- towards medical, conveyance and nourishment charges etc.,
3.
At the time of the accident, petitioner was aged about 11 years and student, due to the said accident, he is completely bed rest, can't sit, squat on the floor, cannot lift or carry weight.

Out of the Shivaram vs Dhananjay.M on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166795074/
2 said accident, crime No.66/2022 is registered before Rajajinagar Police for the offences punishable under Sec.279 and 337 of IPC against driver of the said car.
Respondent No.1 is R.C.Owner and respondent No.3 is insurer of the said car, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
Hence prays to allow the petition and grant the compensation of Rs.8,00,000/- along with interest.
SCCH-5 4.
On service of notice, respondent No.1/owner appeared through person, but not filed written statement.
Respondent No.3 being the insurer has appeared and filed written statement and denied entire averments of the petition.

Further admitted issuance of Digit Commercial Vehicle Package Policy to the Motor Cab bearing Reg.No.KA-54-6329 in favour of respondent No.1 and liability if any, is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.

He is entitled to take shelter under Sec.149(2)
of M.V.Act.
Further submitted that, there is lapse of three days in lodging the complaint.
Further the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving licence and the insured vehicle does not possessed valid permit to ply on the road.
Further submitted that, there was no negligence on the part of driver of the insured vehicle and the sole SCCH-5 negligency is on the part of the petitioner himself.
There is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of M.V.Act.
Claim made by the petitioner is higher, hence his petition is not maintainable.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.
Respondent No.2 has remained absent, hence placed exparte.

5. On going through the rival pleadings of the parties, this tribunal has framed the following:
::ISSUES::

1. Whether the petitioner proves that, on 12.03.2022 at about 5.30 p.m. near 11th Cross, 1st Main, Muneshwara Block, Laggere, Bengaluru he met with accident and sustained grievous injuries, due to rash and negligent driving of driver of Xent Car bearing Reg.No.KA-54-6359?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?
SCCH-5 3.
What order or award?
6. In order to prove the case of the petitioner, father and natural guardian of the petitioner is examined as PW-1 and marked 14 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.14 and closed his evidence.
On the other hand, respondents have not adduced any evidence.

7. Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record,
8.

Then my findings on the above issues are as follows:

3 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following:
SCCH-5 ::REASONS::
9. Issue No.1:-
In order to prove the above Issue No.1, the father and natural guardian of the Petitioner has deposed his evidence as PW-1 by way of reiterating the facts narrated in the petition.
Hence, in order to avoid the repetition of facts, chief- examination of the PW-1 is not reproduced here.

In support of her case, PW-1 has furnished copy of FIR marked as Ex.P.1, copy of charge sheet is marked as Ex.P.2, copy of complaint is marked as Ex.P.3, copy of sketch is marked as Ex.P.4, copy of indemnity bond is marked as Ex.P.7, copy of Sec.133 notice is marked as Ex.P.8.
10.

On perusal of evidence of PW-1 and records those have marked i.e., as FIR, charge sheet,
complaint, sketch, RC, indemnity bond, Sec.133 notice corroborates the case of the petitioner about causing of the accident SCCH-5 dated 12.03.2022 as alleged in the petition and in the evidence of PW-1.
11.

Per contra, except appearance, filing of written statement, respondents have not taken any endeavors to disprove the petitioner's case about non-causing of the accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1.

Since in the absence of iota of evidence, I have no hesitation to believe the case of the petitioner about causing of the injuries to the petitioner out of the accident held on 12.03.2022 at about 5.30 p.m. while petitioner was slowly and cautiously riding the cycle on the 11th Cross, 1st Main, Muneshweara Block, Laggere, Bengaluru.
In the absence of iota of evidence, the arguments advanced by the petitioner's counsel are helpful to the case of the petitioner.
SCCH-5 12.
On the other hand, there is no defence evidence and the police papers speaks that, very accident is occurred due to negligency of the car driver.

Under such circumstances, considering the said evidence and believing the evidence of the petitioner, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that,
PW-1 has proved the above issue No.1 in favour of the petitioner.
Accordingly I have answered above Issue No.1 in the affirmative.
13. Issue No.2:-
As per the case of the Petitioner, he was aged about 11 years as on the date of accident.

In order to prove his age, PW-1 has produced copy of aadhar card of the petitioner marked as Ex.P.10, wherein date of birth of the petitioner is mentioned as 07.01.2012, the alleged accident is occurred on 12.03.2022.
Relying on Ex.P.10 this tribunal has SCCH-5 assessed the age of the petitioner at 11 years as on the date of accident.
14. It is the case of the petitioner that, he has sustained fracture dislocation of right arm and head injury.
To prove the same, PW-1 has produced X-ray Films marked as Ex.P.12, medical bills of Rs.4,740/- marked as Ex.P.13 and OPD records marked as Ex.P.14.

Shivaram vs Dhananjay.M on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166795074/
4 15.
In support of petitioner's case, PW-1 has not examined the Doctor who has given the treatment.
Even he has not produced any wound certificate or discharge summary towards the injuries sustained and treatment taken by the him.

Further as per the admission of PW-1 in his cross-examination, he is guardian of the minor injured, at the time of accident his son was studying in 4th standard and now he is studying in 7th standard and there is no loss of education of the minor child due to SCCH-5 accident.
So as per the own admission of PW-1 out of the accident, minor petitioner has not caused any loss of education and other activities, as such he is not entitled for future loss of income.

Hence petitioner is entitled for global compensation of Rs.50,000/- along with medical expenses of Rs.4,740/-, for which PW-1 has exhibited medical bills marked as Ex.P.13.
16.
Accordingly I hold that, the Petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.54,740/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization of entire amount.

17. In the case on hand, respondent No.3 in favour of respondent No.1 vide its policy No.Do551/9832/21012022 valid since 21.01.2022 to 21.04.2022, the alleged accident was occurred on 12.03.2022 it reveals that, as on the date of accident, SCCH-5 insurance policy was in force.
So that, R3/insurer is directed to deposit the award amount with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. within 60 days from the date of this order.
With these views, I have answered Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.
18. Issue No.3:

For the reasons assigned to Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
::ORDER

: :
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.54,740/- (Rupees Fifty Four Thousand Seven Hundred Forty Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization of entire amount.
SCCH-5
The Respondent No.3 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.

On deposit of compensation amount, entire compensation amount ordered to be kept in Fixed Deposit in any Scheduled Bank in the name of minor Petitioner till he attains age of majority with a liberty to draw accrued interest in the name of minor Petitioner guardian on the said fixed deposit once in 3 months for the benefit of minor Petitioner.
The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
Dictated to the stenographer directly on the computer, typed by her, thereof is corrected and then pronounced by me in the Open Court on this the 3rd day of October, 2024)
(MANJUNATHA K.P.)
